# gyro_dns_acme_key (Resource)

An ACME key of a Gyro DNS service: it can only add and remove _acme-challenge TXT records (Let's Encrypt DNS-01, wildcard certificates), optionally only in `zones` and only from `ips`. Use the token with acme.sh, Certbot, Caddy, Traefik or cert-manager. Every argument forces a new key. The token is known only right after creation (not after import). Requires API 2.13.0.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# ACME key for Let's Encrypt DNS-01 (wildcard certificates). It can only add/remove _acme-challenge TXT records.
resource "gyro_dns_acme_key" "k8s" {
  service_id = 12345 # Gyro DNS service
  name       = "k8s-prod"
  zones      = ["example.com"]
}

# e.g. hand it to cert-manager
resource "kubernetes_secret" "gyro_acme" {
  metadata {
    name      = "gyro-acme"
    namespace = "cert-manager"
  }
  data = { token = gyro_dns_acme_key.k8s.token }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Label, 1-40 characters.
- `service_id` (Number) Gyro DNS service id.

### Optional

- `ips` (Set of String) Client IP addresses allowed to use the key (empty = any).
- `zones` (Set of String) Active zones of the service the key may write in (empty = all zones).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The key (secret).
- `token_prefix` (String) First characters of the key (for display).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <service_id>/<key_id> (the token cannot be recovered after import)
terraform import gyro_dns_acme_key.k8s 12345/67
```
